findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when file is missing, unreadable, or empty.
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path causes process abort instead of returning a typed I/O error the caller can recover from.
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use ? or map_err on fs::read_to_string, with a typed LoadError::Io variant wrapping std::io::Error.

findings.problem: parts[0] indexes into a Vec without bounds checking; line with fewer than 1 comma-separated field panics.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (empty or single-field) causes panic at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: use parts.first().ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or split_once(',') to safely destructure the expected fields.

findings.problem: parts[1] indexes into a Vec without bounds checking; line with exactly 1 field panics.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line missing the value field causes panic at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or split_once(',') to safely destructure the expected fields.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) emits stdout logging inside a data-loading function that should be pure or shell-only.
findings.failure_mode: side-effectful stdout pollutes program output, breaks consumers who parse function results, and couples domain logic to a specific logging backend.
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; move any observation/audit logging to the imperative shell layer outside load_shards, and return a Result so callers can observe success/failure.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates any u32 value above 65535.
findings.failure_mode: a valid 32-bit value such as 70000 silently becomes 4426 in the domain Record, producing silently corrupt data with no error signal.
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) after parsing to u32, or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid).

findings.problem: Record.value is a raw u16 with no invariants; any caller can construct a Record with any u16, including values that are domain-invalid.
findings.failure_mode: illegal domain values propagate through the system unchecked, violating the make-illegal-states-unrepresentable law and making reasoning about invariants impossible.
findings.fix: add a smart constructor or parse-only field: use a private inner field with a public constructor that validates the range, or use a newtype with a fallible parser.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range input.
findings.failure_mode: malformed numeric input (e.g., "abc", "999999") causes process abort instead of returning a typed parse error the caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: replace .unwrap() with .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and propagate via Result, using split_once(',') to destructure the line.

findings.problem: load_shards fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), string parsing, stdout logging, domain construction, and Vec collection into a single function.
findings.failure_mode: violates Data/Calculations/Actions separation; the imperative shell bleeds into domain logic, making the function impossible to test deterministically and impossible to reuse the parsing logic without triggering side effects.
findings.fix: split into a pure parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and a shell load_shards(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that handles I/O and delegates to parse_record.

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper, hiding all failure modes.
findings.failure_mode: every internal failure (I/O error, parse error, index out of bounds, overflow, truncation) must panic rather than returning to the caller as a typed error, violating checked results law.
findings.fix: change signature to pub fn load_shards(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and propagate all fallible operations with ?.

findings.problem: No maximum-items cap, no try_reserve, no input size validation before allocation.
findings.failure_mode: a large or unbounded file exhausts available memory, causing OOM kill or allocation failure panic, violating bounded resources law.
findings.fix: accept a max_items: usize parameter, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? after validating input against the cap, and reject lines exceeding the cap with a typed TooMany error.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() creates a Vec<String> intermediate allocation per line.
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per CSV line adds memory pressure and GC cost; also prevents compile-time shape guarantees (exactly 2 fields expected).
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to destructure into exactly two &str fields without intermediate Vec, then parse directly from the &str slices.
